tool.name: PyEuk distance
tool.description: compute a pairwise genetic-distance matrix from a haplotype sheet
tool.command: pyeuk eukaryotyping --input-sheet '$sheet' --metric $metric --epsilon $epsilon --min-completeness $min_completeness --weight-mode $weight_mode --min-maf $min_maf #if str($ploidy).strip() != '' --ploidy $ploidy #end if #if $fasta --fasta '$fasta' #end if #if not $project_psd --no-psd #end if --output-matrix '$matrix'

param.name: sheet
param.label: Haplotype sheet
param.help: Specimen x haplotype presence/absence sheet, e.g. from the Build haplotype sheet tool.

param.label: Distance metric
param.help: Distance metric. wibs for presence/absence sheets; snp-wibs needs a reference FASTA.

param.label: Allele weighting
param.help: How each haplotype column is weighted. heterozygosity 2p(1-p) suits presence/absence sheets.

param.label: Organism base ploidy
param.help: Organism base ploidy. 1 for haploid, 2 for diploid. Blank uses the engine default.

param.label: Reference / learned FASTA (snp-wibs only)
param.help: Reference or learned FASTA, required only for the snp-wibs metric.

param.label: Minimum locus completeness
param.help: Minimum fraction of loci a specimen must have called to enter the matrix.

param.label: Minimum minor-allele frequency
param.help: Drop a column unless the fraction of called specimens carrying it is between this value and 1 minus it. 0 disables.

param.name: project_psd
param.label: Project onto the PSD cone
param.help: Project the distance matrix onto the PSD cone. Off by default; leave off with a count cut, turn on with a distance cut.

tool.help:
Computes pairwise genetic distances between specimens with a locus-dropout-tolerant, heterozygosity-weighted identity-by-state (wIBS) distance. Surveillance data drop loci unevenly. An unweighted distance over-rewards matches at invariant reference alleles, and a plain Euclidean distance cannot handle missing loci without distortion.
For a pair of specimens the distance is computed strictly over the windows called in both. Each window contributes the weighted absolute difference of its haplotype-presence vectors, divided by locus ploidy (2 for diploid nuclear loci, 1 for mitochondrial or haploid), and the whole is normalised by the summed weights. Each haplotype is weighted by its expected heterozygosity ``w = 2p(1-p)``, where p is its cohort-wide frequency among specimens called at that window, so balanced columns carry the signal and near-invariant ones carry little. Two degenerate cases: a pair sharing no called locus gets distance 1.0; a pair whose shared loci are all invariant gets 0.0.
Ward clustering assumes Euclidean dissimilarity, and locus dropout can make the distance mildly non-Euclidean. ``project_psd`` optionally projects the matrix onto the positive semi-definite cone by clipping negative eigenvalues. Leave it off for count-mode analysis; turn it on for dense distance-mode surveillance.
Output: a square distance matrix, for the cluster tool. @HELP_FOOTER@
